statement0:
The word "degree" is mentioned two or more times in 5.3% of psychology papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "degree" , 25.5% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is a lower rate than the median Psychology paper (median shown in black); relative to other words, papers with "degree" are in the bottom 27th percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better). Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability.
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "degree" tend to be published in lower impact factor journals (40th percentile among all words) but tend to be cited more (53rd percentile word). In general, this word is negatively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are less likely to publish papers containing "degree" (36th percentile).
